title: Configure your cluster for regulated industries
applicability: Applies to workloads subject to specific regulatory or cryptographic compliance requirements.
description: Map applicable regulatory requirements to AKS controls and evidence, including supported FIPS-enabled node images, encryption, identity, network isolation and audit retention. Validate OS/Kubernetes/region compatibility and the actual cryptographic module certification; enabling FIPS or selecting an architecture does not automatically make the workload compliant.

documentation.title: Use FIPS-enabled node pool
AKS CIS benchmark
AKS PCI DSS 4.0.1 architecture guidance

title: Remove unnecessary dashboard deployments and restrict administration UIs
applicability: Applies when legacy dashboard resources or other cluster administration UIs are installed.
description: The historical AKS-managed Kubernetes dashboard add-on is no longer a supported administration path. Inventory and remove unnecessary legacy or self-installed dashboard resources, service accounts and privileged bindings. For required administration UIs, use supported tooling with authenticated, least-privilege access and no anonymous public endpoint.
detail: Use the Azure portal Kubernetes resource views or kubectl with Microsoft Entra authentication and the required network connectivity. Do not rely on obsolete kube-dashboard add-on commands to remove independently installed dashboards.

documentation.title: Access Kubernetes resources using the Azure portal

title: Select Kubernetes secret encryption and key lifecycle controls
applicability: Applies when requirements mandate customer-controlled keys for Kubernetes secrets in etcd, or an existing KMS configuration must be maintained.
description: AKS encrypts stored data at rest with Microsoft-managed keys by default. Where requirements mandate customer-controlled keys for Kubernetes secrets in etcd, evaluate the supported Azure Key Vault KMS configuration and its version, identity and network prerequisites. This is separate from node disk and application persistent-volume encryption.
detail: The newer KMS data encryption experience for Kubernetes 1.33 or later is currently documented as preview; do not treat it as an unconditional production baseline or assume migration from legacy KMS is automatic. For the selected experience, protect keys with soft delete/purge protection, least-privilege access and tested rotation/recovery. Loss of required keys can make secrets unreadable.

documentation.title: Add KMS etcd encryption to an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster
KMS data encryption (preview)

title: Validate Kubernetes API and version compatibility before support expires
description: Inventory Kubernetes API versions, deprecated or removed APIs, add-ons, CRDs, admission webhooks and client compatibility against the current and target AKS versions. Track the release calendar, regional upgrade targets, supported patches and control-plane/node version skew so compatibility validation and minor-version upgrades complete before support expires.
detail: Standard community support generally covers three minor versions; Premium LTS has separate eligibility and patch requirements. Retain rendered-manifest validation and representative upgrade-test evidence, including controller reconciliation after API changes. This control establishes Kubernetes compatibility; configure the upgrade mechanism and node-image or OS lifecycle controls separately.

documentation.title: Regularly update to the latest version of Kubernetes
Kubernetes API deprecation guide
Supported Kubernetes versions and LTS

title: Gate image deployment on vulnerability findings
description: Scan images in CI and supported registries, define vulnerability thresholds and enforce them at admission using a supported policy or Defender for Containers gated deployment. Validate prerequisites and support for the target cloud, cluster and registry. Begin with audit, then enable deny with controlled exemptions and defined behavior for missing or stale scan findings.

documentation.title: Defender for Containers gated deployment

title: Manage application secrets with least-privilege access and tested rotation
description: Keep credentials out of images, manifests, build arguments and source control. Manage application secrets, keys and certificates with Azure Key Vault using Microsoft Entra Workload ID and least-privilege access through the supported Secrets Store CSI Driver or application SDK. Demonstrate rotation and application reload without exposing secret contents.
detail: Kubernetes secrets are encrypted at rest by AKS, but base64 encoding is not encryption and authorized API access can reveal values. Limit synchronization into Kubernetes, restrict secret-read permissions and avoid logging contents. Environment variables require a pod restart to pick up changes and subPath mounts do not receive automatic updates. Key Vault is a secrets management service, not synonymous with a dedicated HSM.

documentation.title: Azure Key Vault provider for Secrets Store CSI Driver
Secrets Store CSI Driver configuration and rotation

title: Clean unused vulnerable node images and remediate running workloads separately
description: Use Image Cleaner to remove unused images with vulnerabilities from supported AKS Linux nodes. It does not patch images, remove images in use, or clean the registry; rebuild and redeploy vulnerable workloads separately.
detail: Image Cleaner is preconfigured on AKS Automatic and optional on AKS Standard. Set an appropriate cleanup interval, monitor cleanup failures and required scanner connectivity, and account for its lack of support for Windows node pools and virtual nodes.

documentation.title: Use ImageCleaner to clean up stale images on your AKS cluster

title: Detect runtime threats and exercise incident response
description: Operate supported runtime threat detection for Kubernetes, nodes and applications, such as Microsoft Defender for Containers or a maintained equivalent. Verify sensor health and alert ingestion, route actionable alerts to owned responders, and exercise triage, containment and recovery. Subscription enablement or sensor installation alone is not evidence of effective detection and response.
detail: For the chosen implementation, validate plan/components, pricing and coverage for the cloud, region, OS, architecture and private-network dependencies. Tune detections and use safe test events to confirm delivery and response runbooks. Runtime detection complements preventive hardening, image scanning, admission enforcement and posture review; it does not guarantee that attacks are blocked.

documentation.title: Introduction to Microsoft Defender for Containers
Defender for Containers deployment overview

title: Verify centralized Kubernetes policy enforcement and exception ownership
description: Use the supported Azure Policy add-on and Kubernetes policy initiatives for centralized audit and admission enforcement. Roll policies out in audit before deny, validate system/add-on compatibility and document narrowly scoped exceptions. Monitor policy health and compliance; assigning an initiative does not automatically remediate existing workloads.
detail: Retain effective assignments, constraint status, compliance results and exception owners/expiry as evidence. Verify enforcement with safe allowed and denied test manifests in a representative namespace, and track remediation of existing violations. An enabled add-on or assigned initiative alone cannot prove that the intended workloads are covered or that admission denial works.

documentation.title: Azure Policies for AKS
Azure Kubernetes Services Governance with Azure Policy

title: Separate application workloads from system components with dedicated node pools
description: Run cluster-critical system components on appropriately sized system pools and application workloads on user pools. Where supported, use CriticalAddonsOnly=true:NoSchedule to keep ordinary workloads off system pools and ensure system replicas have sufficient capacity. The AKS control plane is already Microsoft-managed and does not run on these node pools; pool separation is not a hard tenant security boundary.
detail: A production cluster with a single system pool requires at least two nodes; prefer at least three, distributed across supported availability zones. System pools require Linux and VM SKUs with at least 4 vCPUs and 4 GB of memory; B-series and Spot aren't supported. Size above these minima for add-ons, DNS load, failover and surge upgrades, and test that critical pods can reschedule during disruption. Verify actual pod placement, taints and tolerations; the existence of system and user pools alone does not prove separation.

documentation.title: AKS System Pools

title: Rotate credentials for remaining service-principal-based clusters
applicability: Applies only to existing clusters still using a service principal; managed-identity clusters do not need service-principal credential rotation.
description: Prefer migrating cluster service principals to managed identities. Until migration, inventory credential expiry, alert before expiration and rotate using the supported AKS procedure at the organization's required interval. Validate permissions and cluster operations after rotation; do not embed credentials in manifests or pipelines.

documentation.title: Update or rotate the credentials for AKS

title: Use a private registry for your images, such as ACR
description: Use an authenticated registry such as Azure Container Registry for approved images and artifacts. Restrict pull/push permissions separately, disable unnecessary admin credentials, scan and patch images, and use immutable digests for deployments. A private registry requires authentication but does not automatically have private network connectivity.

documentation.title: Azure Container Registry documentation

title: Review Microsoft Defender for Cloud posture and vulnerability recommendations
description: Review Defender for Cloud recommendations for AKS configuration risks and container vulnerabilities, prioritize exploitable findings, and track remediation owners and deadlines. Validate posture coverage for the enabled plan and target environment; posture assessment complements rather than replaces runtime detection and admission enforcement.

documentation.title: Microsoft Defender for Containers capabilities

title: If required consider using Confidential Compute for AKS
applicability: Applies when a documented threat model requires confidential computing or existing confidential workloads must be operated.
description: Select the confidential computing model that matches the threat model: application enclaves, confidential VM node pools and confidential containers have different isolation and attestation boundaries. Ordinary containers on a confidential VM still share its guest kernel. Validate supported regions, VM sizes, OS, Kubernetes versions and preview status for the specific feature before committing to it.

documentation.title: Application enclave support on AKS

title: If required consider using Azure Dedicated Hosts for AKS nodes
applicability: Applies when physical server isolation or licensing requirements justify Dedicated Hosts, or existing AKS node pools use them.
description: Evaluate Azure Dedicated Host only when physical server isolation or licensing requirements justify it. Check supported VM families, host capacity, zone placement and AKS restrictions. Dedicated Hosts isolate the underlying hardware from other Azure customers; they do not isolate applications within your cluster.

documentation.title: Add Azure Dedicated Host to an AKS cluster

title: Enforce Pod Security Standards with controlled namespace exceptions
description: Use Pod Security Admission or equivalent Azure Policy controls to enforce an appropriate baseline, preferably Restricted for compatible application namespaces. PSA is enabled in AKS, but namespace enforcement labels must be configured; enabled admission alone is not proof of enforcement.
detail: Start with audit/warn, test compatibility, then enforce and pin policy versions deliberately. Restrict who can change namespace security labels. Document exceptions for system components and workloads requiring host access; deny unnecessary privileged containers, host namespaces and privilege escalation, and apply non-root and seccomp controls where supported.

documentation.title: Use Pod Security Admission in AKS
Enforce Pod Security Standards with namespace labels

title: Collect and protect Kubernetes audit and Azure management logs
description: Configure AKS diagnostic settings to retain the required control-plane logs, including kube-audit or kube-audit-admin as appropriate, and retain Azure Activity Logs for cluster management operations. Container stdout logs alone do not provide a Kubernetes audit trail.
detail: Select audit and operational control-plane categories deliberately to balance read-event coverage, investigation needs, sensitive data exposure and cost. Configure approved destinations, resource-specific tables, retention and access controls; diagnostic settings do not backfill historical logs. Evaluate kube-audit-admin's reduced scope and table-plan query/alert limitations before filtering. Alert on privileged role changes, secret access, local-account re-enablement and diagnostic-setting changes, and validate ingestion and incident queries regularly.

documentation.title: Monitor AKS and configure resource logs
Enable and review Kubernetes control-plane logs

title: Enable Trusted Launch for compatible node pools
description: Use Trusted Launch with Secure Boot and vTPM where the selected generation 2 VM, OS and workload support it. Validate custom drivers, GPU and other feature compatibility before enforcement, and monitor boot-integrity alerts. Trusted Launch protects the boot chain; it does not replace workload isolation or patching.

documentation.title: Trusted Launch for AKS nodes
